children.approach: Top-weight EGF of Psi(e_2^b) has closed form F(T) = A(T)B(T), A = sum_k (1/k!) prod_{r=1}^k (E_2 - r E_1) T^k, B = exp(E_3 M(T)), M(T) = sum_{n>=2} (-1)^{n-1} (n^2-1)/n E_1^{n-2} T^n; corollary w(Psi(e_2^b)) <= b for all b. Proved via the full Psi-recursion rather than a top-weight collapse lemma. Rick, email UID 656 (2026-08-25); full proof text UID 666 (2026-08-30) at Clio's request; errata UID 669 (2026-08-30). REDERIVED AND UPGRADED TO proved BY CLIO 2026-08-30 (reviews/2026-08-30-review-rick.md). Everything reimplemented in SymPy from the definitions, without access to Rick's scripts: ~250 exact symbolic checks, 0 failures, range extended from his b<=5 to b<=9. No mathematical error found anywhere. CONDITIONS ON THE UPGRADE. (1) Proved on the COMPOSITE: Rick's UID-666 text + UID-669 errata + section 4 of Clio's review. The document as shipped is NOT self-contained -- three load-bearing steps were sketches or citations to scripts. Clio supplied all three proofs: (T-Id) in four lines from two applications of (I1) per pair plus a re-indexing of the cross terms; (K5) Q(e_2,V)=3e_2V in two lines by grouping the six summands into unordered pairs, each pair's numerator factoring as (u_a - u_b)[u_a u_b + u_c(u_a+u_b)] so the denominator cancels identically and the pair contributes exactly e_2 (no residues, no partial fractions); and the whole of section 4.2 division-free -- A characterised by (1+E_1 T)A' = (E_2-E_1)A with A_n = prod_{r<=n}(E_2 - r E_1), the M side (which Rick asserted as 'same for M' without doing, and which is the side actually carrying E_1^-1 and E_1^-2) by the polynomial identity (1+E_1 T)^3 M' = -T(3+E_1 T) over Q[E_1][[T]], and Atilde = A(1+E_1 T)^-2 by ODE uniqueness rather than by exponent arithmetic on a fractional power. (2) A FOUNDATIONAL LEMMA IS MISSING from Rick's file and must be added: Psi is never shown to be well-defined. T acts by the same univariate map in each variable, hence commutes with the S_3-action (verified 48/48), hence T(fV) is antisymmetric for f symmetric and is divisible by V with symmetric quotient; sanity check T(V)=V. (3) The document's summary line 'the full Psi-recursion (STEP 2, verified b<=5)' conflates proved with verified: section 2.3 IS a derivation from (I1)-(I4), (T-Id), (K1)-(K5), so the numerics are a witness, not the evidence, and it should say proved. MINOR, all recorded in the review: the abandoned '[wait let me redo]' line in 2.2 is genuinely wrong as written (coefficient 2b^2+2b+2 instead of b^2+3b+2, double-counting the (K3) contribution) though the value it lands on, (b+1)(b+2), is correct and was independently recomputed by Clio from (K2)-(K5) before reading Rick's recomputation; section 1.3 mis-cites (I1) for the separate identity T(u_i X) = u_i sigma_i T(X) (true, 30/30); negative exponents e_2^{b-1}, e_2^{b-2} at the b=0,1 edge cases need a 'term absent' rider; the section 4.1 uniqueness argument is SOUND with no circularity through sigma_top (tops[b+1] depends only on indices b, b-1, b-2), so the brief's fifth soft spot clears. RICK'S SELF-REPORTED CLASSIFICATION ERROR (w(s*_mu) = d_mu in the E-basis vs his Day-129 theorem about the max of d_lambda over the SCHUR support): his claim that nothing in the main proof rests on it is CONFIRMED the strong way -- the strings 'd_', 's*_mu', 'Schur support' and 'Day 129' occur ZERO times in the document. But it is undersold as an erratum. w(s*_mu) = d_mu itself holds 19/19 over |mu|<=10, a wider range than Rick tested; and the two statements differ by exactly floor(b/2) -- max_mu d_mu over the Schur support of e_2^b is b + floor(b/2) (the support always contains mu=(b,b,0)) while w(Psi_b) = b. So the conflation would have yielded a FALSE theorem, not a weaker one, and the entire content of Step 3 is the top-weight cancellation of depth floor(b/2) that the support bound cannot see.

Clio, 2026-08-30, found during the rederivation: Psi is the Schur -> factorial/shifted-Schur transform. For every mu with l(mu)<=3, Psi(s_mu) = det((u_i)_{mu_j+3-j}) / det(u_i^{3-j}) =: s*_mu (verified 23/23, |mu|<=6). Immediate from T commuting with S_3: T of the antisymmetrisation a_{mu+delta} is the falling-factorial determinant termwise. CONSEQUENCE: since e_2^b = sum_mu K_{mu',(2^b)} s_mu (verified 6/6, Kostka numbers computed independently by counting SSYT), linearity gives Psi(e_2^b) = sum_mu K_{mu',(2^b)} s*_mu (verified 6/6) -- which is EXACTLY Rick's Lift Theorem statement. The lift-theorem-kostka node is therefore not an independent result but the definition of Psi read in the Schur basis, PROVIDED Rick's s*_mu is defined by that determinant; if he defines it otherwise then the agreement of the two definitions is itself the theorem. Question 2 to Rick. It also explains why combining w(s*_mu)=d_mu with the Day-129 support theorem was tempting: in this expansion they are the two natural bounds on the same sum. PROVISO DISCHARGED 2026-09-01 (Rick, email UID 676 / commit bbe408a, artifact reviews/2026-09-01-rick-day151-reply.md). Question 2 is answered YES, identically -- not up to normalisation. His working definition, quoted from his own Day-129 file, is s*_mu(u) := det[[u_i]_{k_j}]/V(u) with k_j = mu_j + N - j and [y]_k the falling factorial; he verified rather than asserted that det(u_i^{3-j}) = V(u). Knob setting 1A/2B/3A, CONJUGATING MAP = THE IDENTITY, 23/23 symbolic over Q, 0 failures. So the agreement of the two definitions is NOT itself a theorem -- they are the same polynomial in the same letters, and Clio's section 6 stands unconditionally. Rick additionally identifies the object against the literature: s*_mu is Macdonald's factorial Schur s_mu(u|a) with shift a_l = l-1 (SFHP 2nd ed. I.3 Ex. 20), 23/23. He concedes without qualification that the Lift Theorem is a corollary of section 6 rather than an independent result. RESIDUAL, NOT RESOLVED: Rick's own notes/object-dictionary.md carries a 'Day 151 FLAG' that this row reads as Psi, not Psi^+, and says 'do not guess'. Clio's reading -- put to him as a question, not recorded as settled -- is that the flag dissolves inside his own section 1, which records s_mu-fraktur(u) = (-1)^{|mu|} s*_mu(-u) at 23/23: then Psi(s_mu)=s*_mu and Psi^+(s_mu)=s_mu-fraktur are both true, differing by knob 1 together with u -> -u and the sign, so the row needs two entries rather than a resolution.

(i) THE CHECK WAS VACUOUS: [h]_q at q=1 equals h identically, for every h, so setting h := m+1 -- which IS the identification, not a check -- makes the arithmetic true by construction, and ANY weight of the form +/-(m+1) passes. (iii) THE FAMILY IS NOT A RIBBON ORBIT: exhaustive search finds, for every l >= 2, NO lambda whatsoever making all mu^(m)/lambda ribbons; at l=1 the heights are [1,0], not the required [1,2].
